title: Machine Learning Topological Order from Defect Partition Functions
authors: Kazem Bitaghsir Fadafan, Wei Cui, Babak Haghighat, Shailesh Lal
abstract: We introduce a machine learning framework for extracting Ising topological order from defect partition functions of the two-dimensional Ising model on a torus. Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) are trained on Ising model data sampled at criticality across topological sectors. We take a component-wise square-root map of the learned distributions which naturally produces candidate wavefunctions for the (2+1)-dimensional Ising TQFT. As a nontrivial consistency check, we extract the modular S-matrix from overlaps of the resulting states and recover the expected Ising modular data. Our results demonstrate that neural network representations can capture both critical fluctuations and emergent topological structure, providing a data-driven route from lattice statistical mechanics to topological quantum field theory.
summary: The paper introduces an innovative machine learning approach using Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) to extract the underlying Topological Quantum Field Theory structure from the critical 2D Ising model. By training RBMs on lattice configurations, the authors successfully map classical partition functions onto quantum wavefunctions whose overlaps correctly predict fundamental topological invariants like the modular S-matrix.
main_problem: The research aims to develop a machine learning framework to extract the topological order inherent in the 2D Ising model from its defect partition functions.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated that Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) can learn representations whose overlaps reproduce the expected modular S-matrix of the Ising Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT).
method: They train RBMs on Monte Carlo samples from the critical 2D Ising model, using a component-wise square-root map to generate candidate wavefunctions for the TQFT.
model_or_system: The physical system is the two-dimensional Ising model defined on a torus ($T^2$), analyzed at its critical point. The theoretical framework connects this lattice statistical mechanics problem to $(2+1)$-dimensional Ising TQFTs via duality transformations and defect insertions.
key_observables: Modular S-matrix elements, partition functions $Z_{L_1 L_2}$, Binder cumulant ($U_4(m)$), and RBM reconstruction error ($	ext{Erecon}$).
important_parameters: Critical coupling constant ($K_c$), temperature/coupling parameters, and the modular parameter $	au$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the underlying physics (Ising TQFT) can be accurately captured by training an RBM on classical lattice samples. A limitation noted is the inability to learn complex phase information.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometric relationship between dual lattices, heatmaps of weight covariance matrices ($\Sigma = WWT$) showing defect-induced couplings, and visualizations of eigenmodes derived from the learned Hamiltonian.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by reviewing lattice duality (KW), introducing defects via gauge fields, establishing connections to CFT characters using transfer matrices, and finally proposing the RBM mapping technique for computational extraction of topological invariants.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, data-driven methodology—using deep learning—to tackle fundamental problems in condensed matter theory concerning emergent quantum order and topological phases, bridging statistical mechanics with advanced ML techniques.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Geometric configuration of the two-dimensional Ising model on the primary lattice Λ (blue sites) and its corresponding dual lattice ˜Λ (green sites). Dashed and dotted lines denote horizontal and vertical edges on Λ, respectively. Each dual site ˜p ∈˜Λ is positioned at the center of its associated primary plaquette, shifting it by (+1/2, +1/2) relative to the primary site p ∈Λ, which effectively rotates the dual edge axes by 45◦relative to the primary lattice.

Figure 2: Lattice realization of the non-invertible Kramers-Wannier duality defect line. The seam acts as a topological interface matching the primary Hilbert space H (blue sites) with the dual Hilbert space ˆH (yellow sites), enforcing the non-local duality-twisted boundary conditions across the cycle.

Figure 3: Lattice configuration of a vertical Z2 spin-flip defect line. The defect is implemented by executing a local gauge transformation that systematically inverts the signs of the vertical bond couplings (Ky 7→−Ky) along the highlighted red cut-line switching ferromagnetic interactions across the bond to anti-ferromagnetic. Blue dots represent the primary lattice sites and yellow dots are the dual lattice sites

Figure 4: Monte Carlo samples of the Ising model on a 64 × 64 lattice, collected from the four spin-flip defect sectors corresponding to Z1 1,1, Zψ 1,ψ, Zψ ψ,1 and Z1 ψ,ψ, where we are reading the rows top to bottom . Higher temperatures are shown in columns to the left. The snapshots provide some visual indication of how the antiferromagnetic seam insertion, dominant at low temperatures is negligible in the high temperature limit.
Figure 5: Rescaled susceptibility computed near criticality for the Ising model at varying β, L. The plots coalesce over each other, a feature of scale invariance near criticality.
